operation_details.item: The user uses cost-plus pricing for one product line.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Hey, do you have a minute to go over the pricing updates? I'm trying to make sure I'm consistent across the product lines.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Sure, I've got time. I recall you've been documenting everything in the pricing guide—what's changed?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: I'm just reviewing the different approaches we use. For the platform, we stick with value-based pricing, and for the entry tier, we're using competitor-based pricing. The legacy widgets line is still on cost-plus pricing.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Got it, so three different models depending on the product. That's all captured in the pricing guide, right?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. The guide lays it all out so the team doesn't mix them up. It's been helpful when we're putting together client proposals.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That makes sense. How have clients been reacting to the value-based approach on the platform?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Pretty well, actually. They can see the ROI clearly. The cost-plus line feels more stable but less strategic in comparison.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's useful context. Let me know if you need any help refining the guide or tweaking the messaging for any of those tiers.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Forget only that I use cost-plus pricing, while keeping the value-based and competitor-based approaches and the guide.
